work.title: The Life of Timon of Athens
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 3, Scene 3
scene.title: SCENE III. The same. A room in Sempronius' house
scene.location: The same. A room in Sempronius' house

content.text: Enter a Third Servant of Timon's with Sempronius, another of Timon's friends.

lines.text: Must he needs trouble me in't? Hum! 'Bove all others?
lines.plainText: Must he needs trouble me in't Hum 'Bove all others

lines.text: He might have tried Lord Lucius or Lucullus;
lines.plainText: He might have tried Lord Lucius or Lucullus

lines.text: And now Ventidius is wealthy too,
lines.plainText: And now Ventidius is wealthy too

lines.text: Whom he redeemed from prison. All these
lines.plainText: Whom he redeemed from prison All these

lines.text: Owe their estates unto him.
lines.plainText: Owe their estates unto him

lines.text: My lord,
lines.plainText: My lord

lines.text: They have all been touched and found base metal,
lines.plainText: They have all been touched and found base metal

lines.text: For they have all denied him.
lines.plainText: For they have all denied him

lines.text: How? Have they denied him?
lines.plainText: How Have they denied him

lines.text: Has Ventidius and Lucullus denied him
lines.plainText: Has Ventidius and Lucullus denied him

lines.text: And does he send to me? Three? Humh!
lines.plainText: And does he send to me Three Humh

lines.text: It shows but little love or judgment in him.
lines.plainText: It shows but little love or judgment in him

lines.text: Must I be his last refuge? His friends, like physicians,
lines.plainText: Must I be his last refuge His friends like physicians

lines.text: Thrive, give him over. Must I take th' cure upon me?
lines.plainText: Thrive give him over Must I take th' cure upon me

lines.text: Has much disgraced me in't. I'm angry at him,
lines.plainText: Has much disgraced me in't I'm angry at him

lines.text: That might have known my place. I see no sense for't
lines.plainText: That might have known my place I see no sense for't

lines.text: But his occasions might have wooed me first;
lines.plainText: But his occasions might have wooed me first

lines.text: For, in my conscience, I was the first man
lines.plainText: For in my conscience I was the first man

lines.text: That e'er received gift from him.
lines.plainText: That e'er received gift from him

lines.text: And does he think so backwardly of me now
lines.plainText: And does he think so backwardly of me now

lines.text: That I'll requite it last? No.
lines.plainText: That I'll requite it last No

lines.text: So it may prove an argument of laughter
lines.plainText: So it may prove an argument of laughter

lines.text: To th' rest, and I 'mongst lords be thought a fool.
lines.plainText: To th' rest and I 'mongst lords be thought a fool

lines.text: I'd rather than the worth of thrice the sum
lines.plainText: I'd rather than the worth of thrice the sum

lines.text: Had sent to me first, but for my mind's sake;
lines.plainText: Had sent to me first but for my mind's sake

lines.text: I'd such a courage to do him good. But now return,
lines.plainText: I'd such a courage to do him good But now return

lines.text: And with their faint reply this answer join:
lines.plainText: And with their faint reply this answer join

lines.text: Who bates mine honour shall not know my coin.
lines.plainText: Who bates mine honour shall not know my coin

lines.text: Excellent! Your lordship's a goodly villain. The devil knew not what he did when he made man politic; he crossed himself by't, and I cannot think but, in the end the villainies of man will set him clear. How fairly this lord strives to appear foul! Takes virtuous copies to be wicked, like those that under hot ardent zeal would set whole realms on fire.
lines.plainText: Excellent Your lordship's a goodly villain The devil knew not what he did when he made man politic he crossed himself by't and I cannot think but in the end the villainies of man will set him clear How fairly this lord strives to appear foul Takes virtuous copies to be wicked like those that under hot ardent zeal would set whole realms on fire

lines.text: Of such a nature is his politic love.
lines.plainText: Of such a nature is his politic love

lines.text: This was my lord's best hope, now all are fled
lines.plainText: This was my lord's best hope now all are fled

lines.text: Save only the gods. Now his friends are dead,
lines.plainText: Save only the gods Now his friends are dead

lines.text: Doors that were ne'er acquainted with their wards
lines.plainText: Doors that were ne'er acquainted with their wards

lines.text: Many a bounteous year must be employed
lines.plainText: Many a bounteous year must be employed

lines.text: Now to guard sure their master.
lines.plainText: Now to guard sure their master

lines.text: And this is all a liberal course allows,
lines.plainText: And this is all a liberal course allows

lines.text: Who cannot keep his wealth must keep his house.
lines.plainText: Who cannot keep his wealth must keep his house
